drivingQuestion: From where does the mother have property of her own?
outcomeNote: Answered; the answer is challenged in the next unit.

segments.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיִּגְנוֹב מִשֶּׁל אָבִיו וּמִשֶּׁל אִמּוֹ. אִמּוֹ מְנָא לַהּ? מַה שֶּׁקָּנְתָה אִשָּׁה קָנָה בַּעְלָהּ! אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מִסְּעוּדָה הַמּוּכֶנֶת לְאָבִיו וּלְאִמּוֹ.
segments.en: The mishna teaches that «Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says» that he is not liable as a stubborn and rebellious son «unless he steals» that which belonged «to his father and» that which belonged «to his mother.» The Gemara asks: With regard to «his mother, from where does she have» independently owned property that her son can steal? The basis for this question is the halakha that «anything that a woman acquires is acquired by her husband. Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says» in answer to this question: The mishna is referring to a case where the boy stole food «from a meal that had been prepared for his father and for his mother.» In such a case the husband grants his wife ownership of the food that she will eat over the course of her meal.
